editorial:
Imagine waking up in a place where everything you know about power is flipped upside down. You follow a guy named Snaporaz who thinks he is a smooth talker, but he quickly finds out he is out of his league. After chasing a mysterious woman, he stumbles into a hotel full of women attending a feminist convention. The vibe is wild, colorful, and totally unpredictable. It feels less like a normal story and more like a strange, funny dream where the rules change every five minutes. You will feel Snaporaz's confusion as he tries to navigate this world where he is the one being judged and stared at.

The acting is loud and expressive, which makes the comedy land well, even if the pacing feels a bit slow in some spots. You might find some parts a bit too weird, but that is the point of the experience. If you enjoy movies that feel like a carnival, you will love this.
endingExplained: By the end, the line between reality and dreams totally disappears. Snaporaz realizes he is trapped in a fantasy world created by his own desires and fears. Instead of escaping, he becomes part of the chaos. The movie wraps up with a giant, theatrical parade of women, showing that he has been completely swallowed by this strange land. He never truly finds the woman from the train because she was just a trigger for this wild trip.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves surreal stories and artistic films.
